RM0522 p382 explicitly supports memory/peripheral in all four source/destination combinations; per-channel completion/half/error/suspend events. This is hardware support, not proof of arbitrary endpoint safety or dual handshakes.
RM0522 Table86: C53xxx/C542xx have four channels0..3 on each LPDMA1/2; larger variants differ. All LPDMA instances/channels connect the same supported request/trigger set. LPDMA has no FIFO.
RM0522 Table90: SPI1 RX/TX request selectors4/5 and I2C1 RX/TX10/11. LPDMA2 has no FIFO. Request selection alone does not prove peripheral presence on every part.
RM0522 Table90: USART2 RX/TX selectors14/15; channel request availability must be intersected with exact part presence.

RM0522 Table91 lists only lptim1_ue_dma as block request. Table92 PFREQ early termination is limited to channels0/7; combining this with C542 channel presence in Table86 leaves channel0 on each controller.
RM0522 linked-list base/address rules require all linked-list nodes in the same64Kbyte address window. Linked-list execution is documented, not implemented by the direct-transfer cards.
RM0522 source/destination widths support1/2/4 bytes;8-byte width is not supported. Source/destination addresses must align to respective widths; increment is contiguous or fixed.
RM0522 supports padding/truncation/sign extension between widths, not packing multiple source cells. Current direct-transfer implementation domain uses equal widths only.

RM0522 prohibits the same active peripheral request on multiple active channels without automatic error detection. SWREQ1 generates software requests; with SWREQ0 the first memory read is gated by the selected hardware request whether the peripheral is source or destination. The described request mechanism does not establish arbitrary endpoint-pair readiness.
RM0522 documents four priority levels with arbitration per single atomic read/write transfer. Priority does not certify an application latency or bandwidth.
RM0522 describes circular buffering using a linked-list reload of block size and memory address. Direct-transfer cards are finite blocks and do not implement circular mode.
RM0522 documents separate enable bits/flags for channel completion, half completion, data/user/link/trigger errors and suspend; event flag state is separate from interrupt enable.

RM0522 channel privilege controls source/destination/link accesses; data-transfer errors stop the channel and require channel reset before reuse. Bus reachability alone does not establish access rights.
RM0522 trigger overrun flag does not automatically disable the channel. Direct cards do not enable hardware triggers; triggered profiles need explicit overrun handling.
RM0522 CBR1 BNDT source-byte count is16bits; a nonzero count must be a multiple of source width or a user-setting error occurs.

RM0522 p89 LPDMA bus targets Flash, SRAM1/2 and AHB peripheral bridges. This family bus statement does not establish all peripherals, security/privilege settings, cache coherence or any arbitrary address on C542.

ES0676 SPI slave RDY-output high-clock limitation is outside master/internal-NSS profile; not a complete SPI system qualification.

Allocation only; no component is generated. resource_bindings gives the timer's hal_instance and clock_enable_api, the pad's port_symbol, pin_symbol and clock_enable_api, and under routes the selected signal with its alternate_symbol and channel_symbol. The application enables the TIM module if no other selected card does (USE_HAL_TIM_MODULE in generated/hal/stm32c5xx_hal_conf.h and stm32c5xx_drivers/hal/stm32c5xx_hal_tim.c in CMakeLists.txt), enables both clocks, initializes the pad with mode HAL_GPIO_MODE_ALTERNATE and the route's alternate_symbol, and drives the channel through the SDK TIM API in stm32c5xx_hal_tim.h starting from HAL_TIM_Init with the allocated hal_instance. Period, duty, polarity, compare or capture mode, complementary outputs, dead time and break are application decisions. One counter serves all channels, so the allocation takes the whole timer. No timing, electrical or errata qualification.

Allocation only; no component is generated. resource_bindings gives the converter's hal_instance and clock_enable_api, the pad's port_symbol, pin_symbol and clock_enable_api, and under routes the selected signal with its channel_symbol. The application enables the ADC module (USE_HAL_ADC_MODULE in generated/hal/stm32c5xx_hal_conf.h and stm32c5xx_drivers/hal/stm32c5xx_hal_adc.c in CMakeLists.txt), enables both clocks, initializes the pad with mode HAL_GPIO_MODE_ANALOG, and configures and reads the converter through the SDK ADC API in stm32c5xx_hal_adc.h starting from HAL_ADC_Init with the allocated hal_instance. The converter is one shared unit: sequencing of several inputs, sampling time, calibration, reference voltage and accuracy are application decisions. Internal channels, injected and differential conversion are not covered. Only the pad each input uses without the SBS pin remap is offered: PC4, PC5, PB0 and PB1 need the SBS pin remap and are excluded, so no remap is required. Not together with analog_reading on the same converter: its generated units own the converter's configuration. The two hold the converter in different ownership modes, so a request with both on one converter is refused, and the refusal names the converter under ownership_conflicts. No electrical or errata qualification.

Generated component owns the timer handle, the time base, one compare unit in PWM mode 1 with preload, the channel and the pad. Use the returned interface; do not initialize the timer, the channel or the pad again. Supports only the listed frequencies at the captured 144MHz kernel clock: each has an exact prescaler and period, the period is at least 1000 counts and full duty fits a 16-bit compare register. Duty is thousandths of the period rounded down to a whole count; the duty in force from a period boundary on is the last one written before it. The first period after a start can be shorter at the pad; that it is not longer follows from the order of the calls and is not measured. start and stop belong to one thread; set duty may also run in an interrupt. Init verifies the clock and register factors; dynamic clock changes are outside the contract. Build is not a measurement of frequency, duty or edge quality.

implementations.guidance: Generated component. The first unit on a converter sets the ADC and DAC kernel clock to HCLK divided by 8 (18MHz in the captured 144MHz profile) before it enables the converter's bus clock, reads the clock configuration back, sets 12-bit resolution, software trigger and one conversion per request, activates the converter and runs its offset calibration; every unit on that converter shares the one handle, and each unit switches its own pad to analog mode. Use the returned interface; do not initialize the converter, its clock or the pad again. The units own the converter: do not combine them with an analog_input_pin allocation on the same converter. The two hold the converter in different ownership modes, so a request that makes that combination is refused, and the refusal names the converter under ownership_conflicts. read converts once with the SDK's longest sampling time and returns counts 0..4095, right aligned: a fraction of VREF+, not volts, because the reference is not measured. Before each conversion the unit checks on the converter itself that it is enabled, idle and holds this input; it selects its input again when another is held, which stops, switches, starts and calibrates the converter, and it reports HAL_ERROR for good when the converter was stopped or is converting behind it. Every wait is the SDK's and is counted in HAL ticks, which must be advancing: 2ms for a conversion; on a switch 2ms each to stop, disable and enable and 228ms for calibration, about a quarter of a second in all before an error. One thread only, never from an interrupt. The same kernel clock feeds the DAC. No internal channels, injected or differential conversion, triggers, interrupts, DMA, oversampling or analog watchdog. PC4, PC5, PB0 and PB1 need the SBS pin remap and are excluded. Accuracy, source impedance and noise are not qualified; build is not a measurement.

implementations.guidance: Generated component owns the timer handle, a 1MHz time base over a 16-bit period, capture of both edges on the allocated channel's own pin, the compare flag of the other of the timer's first two channels as a half-turn mark (that channel drives no pad), and the pad as an input with the selected pull. Use the returned interface; do not initialize the timer, a channel or the pad again. measure waits for a rising edge, the falling edge after it and the next rising edge and returns period and high time in whole microseconds of the timer clock. The time limit, 1..60000 ms, is counted on the same clock from the call: HAL_TIMEOUT when the edges have not occurred by then, and an edge at or after the limit is not used. The unit polls: it must look at the timer at least every 32.768ms to follow the 16-bit counter. A thread held longer than that between two looks may get HAL_ERROR and one held for 65.536ms or more always does; edges closer together than the loop can follow also give HAL_ERROR, through the overcapture flag or a capture found waiting. A measurement is never completed from a count the unit could not follow, and a held thread delays the return by the time it was held. One thread only, never from an interrupt. No input filter, prescaled capture, interrupt or DMA capture or XOR input. Init verifies the clock and register factors for the pinned 144MHz profile; times are counts of the nominal clock, not measured against a reference.

implementations.guidance: Generated component owns the watchdog handle. Generated init only prepares it: the application calls start when it is ready, and from then on must call refresh within the reset time or the microcontroller resets. The watchdog cannot be stopped or reconfigured before a reset, so start it only when the refresh path is in place. The reset time is the selected number of milliseconds at the nominal 32kHz of the low-speed internal oscillator; timeout_ms reports the time the driver set, and the oscillator's real frequency shifts it. The SDK enables the watchdog before it waits for its registers, and those waits can fail: when start returns an error other than busy, state reports 2, the watchdog may be running with a reset time that is not known, timeout_ms reports 0xFFFFFFFF, refresh still restarts the count, start cannot be tried again, and a reset may follow. No window (a refresh is allowed at any time) and no early interrupt. refresh may be called from the owning thread or an interrupt; start from the thread only. Behaviour while a debugger halts the core and in low-power modes, and the option bytes, are not covered. Build does not exercise the reset.

Any other result is a failed start after which the watchdog may be running with a reset time that is not known: state is 2 and a reset may follow. Thread only.
interface.refresh: {{unit}}_refresh(): checked HAL_OK restarts the count; call it more often than the reset time. Thread or interrupt. HAL_ERROR before any start; after a failed start the count is restarted all the same.
interface.timeout: {{unit}}_timeout_ms(): the reset time the driver set, in milliseconds of the nominal oscillator; 0 before start; 0xFFFFFFFF after a failed start, when it is not known.
interface.scope: No window, no early interrupt, nominal 32kHz oscillator. The reset time is not measured, the reset is not exercised by a build, and a failed start is not recoverable.
